correctness.rationale: The twelve cube edges were independently reconstructed by one-bit XOR. A separate vertex-based maximum-matching DP on all 4096 edge masks gives face counts 45, 601, 2665 including the empty face for k=2,3,4. Independently implementing the supplied pivot permutations and all oriented nonempty Hasse covers yields respectively 19/295/1331 matched pairs, 72/2184/13884 cover arrows and complete DAG topological sorting. Removing the augmented empty-face pair leaves exactly (critical d0:1,d1:5), (d0:1,d3:9), (d0:1,d5:1). Each is a legitimate finite acyclic discrete-Morse matching, hence an integral CW model with just one vertex and a single higher-cell dimension, forcing the claimed wedges; mod-2 ranks in the source file provide corroboration but not the integral proof. At k=1 there are only the empty face; a cube perfect matching has size four, so all k>=5 give an 11-simplex. Since positive homology appears only in successive degrees 1,3,5 and transitions are by inclusion, each stage class dies at the next threshold, yielding exactly five [2,3), nine [3,4) and one [4,5) positive-degree integral bars. The result is exact only for Q3; no extrapolation to higher cubes.

evidence: Linusson–Shareshian–Welker prove NM_k(K_{r,s}) is a wedge of binomial(r-1,k-1)binomial(s-1,k-1) spheres of dimension 2k-3; K4,4 has ranks (9,9,1), whereas Q3 has k=2 rank five.
Holmsen–Lee show all bipartite NM_k(G) have vanishing reduced field homology above degree 2k-3, but do not determine low degrees or Q3 sphere multiplicities.
Shan–Lu–Wang v2 gives top-degree injectivity under bipartite edge addition and a nonzero top class when a cycle length at least 2k exists, not an exact integral homotopy classification.
The Heawood result classifies another specific 21-edge graph and does not imply this 12-edge graph.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The complete bipartite wedge theorem applies to the complete ambient graph and cannot be substituted for the induced subcomplex on the cube edges; its first rank already disagrees. The general vanishing/injectivity results are weaker than a complete integral homotopy type. The k=4 field Betti rank one is partially implied by the 8-cycle injection plus upper rank one in K4,4; this prior implication is explicitly credited, but it does not yield the k=3 rank or either k=3/k=4 integral attaching maps.

evidence: The k=2 five-circle result is also an elementary nerve-lemma consequence: NM2(Q3) is the union of eight simplices of edges incident to each cube vertex; nerve Q3 has first Betti number 12−8+1=5.

For k=4, injection from an 8-cycle to Q3 and from Q3 to K4,4 together with the known K4,4 rank one implies a one-dimensional top homology over a field; this does not establish its full integral homotopy type.
At k=3 the complete bipartite top homology rank nine gives an upper bound, but source results do not show equality for Q3 or vanishing of every other integral group.
Direct exhaustive acyclic matchings yield critical CW cells (0:1,1:5), (0:1,3:9), (0:1,5:1), proving the full wedge types rather than assuming field Betti numbers imply them.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Prior results partially cover the elementary k=2 stage and top-field rank for k=4, so those numerical facts are not claimed as independent first discoveries. The substantive complete classification, especially the k=3 integral wedge, k=4 integral homotopy and all-stage certified filtration, does not follow from the examined theorem implications.

evidence: Binary parity classes show Q3 is isomorphic to the four-crown K_{4,4} minus its antipodal perfect matching.

originality.rationale: The complete-bipartite homotopy formula gives K4,4 ranks (9,9,1), while Q3 is K4,4 minus a perfect matching and has first rank 5. Holmsen–Lee proves vanishing bounds for arbitrary bipartite G, and Shan–Lu–Wang prove top-field injectivity and cycle nonvanishing; these do not imply the full cube homotopy classification or exact k=3 rank. A familiar nerve lemma already gives the k=2 stage, and the k=4 top FIELD rank follows from an 8-cycle and injection into K4,4; those partial implications are explicitly credited. The outstanding precise Q3 k=3 integral wedge, k=4 integral homotopy and complete filtration have not been located in the primary results or published record comparisons. This is best-of-knowledge originality with unindexed equivalence risk, not proof of priority.
residual_risks: Priority remains a best-of-knowledge assessment; an unindexed exact four-crown computation or broader theorem might exist.

The k=2 homotopy follows from a standard good-cover nerve calculation and the k=4 top field rank is already constrained exactly by prior injection and complete-bipartite results; novelty is therefore limited to the complete integral filtration, notably k=3 and homotopy refinements.

value.rationale: The cube is a canonical three-dimensional hypercube and four-crown, naturally just one perfect-matching deletion from the complete bipartite graph where full nonmatching topology is known. The complete threshold-by-threshold INTEGRAL homotopy classification is a natural exact invariant of this particular graph complex, not an arbitrary hand-picked computation. Its nine three-spheres and verified higher-stage sphere distinction, combined with the changed first multiplicity and complete persistence bar pattern, provide a reproducible benchmark for graph-complex topology; a researcher comparing sparse bipartite graphs to the complete case could need this precise answer. The elementary first stage and field-level top rank are prior/standard, so no novelty or value is claimed for those isolated facts, nor for a general family theorem.
